ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a transition-state structure, with one benzene ring on each of the left and right sides, and a fused central ring in the middle; above there is an H connected to the central carbon; the lower central carbon is connected to R and OH2+, and there are also several curved arrows in the figure. According to the problem statement, ignore arrows and exclude bonds involving hydrogen. Reasoning: The left benzene ring provides 6 C-C bonds; the right benzene ring provides 6 C-C bonds. In the central ring, the edges fused with the two benzene rings are already included in the benzene-ring count, so only 4 unrepeated C-C bonds are additionally counted for the central ring. The lower central carbon also has two non-hydrogen substituent bonds: C-R and C-OH2, each counted as 1. Exclude the upper C-H bond and the O-H bonds in OH2. Total = 6 + 6 + 4 + 2 = 18.

method.method_draft: Count by structural regions: the left benzene ring contributes 6 C-C bonds, the right benzene ring contributes 6 C-C bonds. The central ring adds only the 4 C-C bonds not already counted as fused benzene edges. Then add the two non-hydrogen substituent bonds at the lower central carbon: C-R and C-OH2. Total = 6 + 6 + 4 + 2 = 18.

method.method_draft: Assign non-hydrogen degrees from the drawn skeleton. Each benzene unit has four ordinary carbons of degree 2 and two fused carbons of degree 3, so each side contributes degree sum 4×2 + 2×3 = 14; both sides give 28. The top central carbon has two non-H connections, the lower central carbon has four non-H connections, the OH2 oxygen contributes one C-O connection, and the R substituent endpoint contributes one connection. Degree sum = 28 + 2 + 4 + 1 + 1 = 36, so bonds = 36/2 = 18.
